title: Wiring Beans: @Autowired and Constructor Injection
description: Connect your beans together using Spring’s automatic wiring.

slides.title: The Missing Link: @Autowired 🧵
slides.content:
# Telling Spring to Inject

Once you have beans, you need to tell Spring where to inject them. The primary way is using `@Autowired`.

**However**, since Spring 4.3, if a class has a **single constructor**, you can omit `@Autowired` – Spring will use that constructor automatically. This is the modern, cleanest approach.

quizData.question: Which injection type does Spring prefer when a class has only one constructor?
quizData.explanation: Since Spring 4.3, if a bean has a single constructor, Spring automatically uses it for injection, even without @Autowired.

slides.title: What Just Happened? ✨
slides.content:
# Spring Did the Magic

1. It found `GreetingService` because it’s annotated with `@Service`.
2. It found `GreetingController` because it’s `@RestController` (which is `@Component`).
3. It saw the constructor in `GreetingController` taking a `GreetingService`.
4. It looked up the `GreetingService` bean and passed it in.

No `new` keywords, no factory classes – just clean, testable code.

slides.title: Testing the Controller 🧪
slides.content: Because we used constructor injection, writing a unit test is easy: we can pass a mock `GreetingService` to the controller’s constructor, without needing to start Spring.
